summary.en: An active buzzer on a three-pin board. Boards differ: some sound when S is HIGH, others when S is LOW; the lab has a setting for each.

simplified: The buzzer is a resistor that sounds above a threshold voltage.
A board that sounds on LOW is modelled with the buzzer between + and S, so S carries the buzzer's current; a real board switches it with a transistor, so S carries only a few milliamps.
